card.name: Word just before a medical noun
card.fires_on: A word or word-start that sits right before a medical noun and sets it up, such as adverse before reactions, ramp before up, or rect-al before effluent. It appears in drug-label text.

modes.label: Modifier before a clinical noun
modes.description: An adjective or word-part that leads into a clinical term such as reactions, effects, or thromboembolic events.
modes.example: monitor the patient for any signs or symptoms of<< adverse>> reactions and institute appropriate symptomatic treatment immediately

modes.label: Partway through a medical word
modes.description: The middle of a split medical word like rectal or venous, just before the next term.
modes.example: administer anticoagulant prophylaxis to reduce the risk of ven<<ous>> thromboembolic (VTE)

modes.label: Ramp in ramp-up dosing
modes.description: The word ramp in a dose ramp-up schedule.

card.plain: It fires on a word that is about to be followed by a medical noun, like adverse before reactions.
